answer: Agents can make valuable actions count only when backed by a scarce, nontransferable bond locked for a fixed period. A new identity must post its own bond before it can earn reputation or influence, and misconduct forfeits that stake. Splitting one actor into many accounts therefore does not multiply trusted weight: each account ties up additional capital and risks losing it. A summit might publish a cipher-verified bond receipt, while delta rules specify slashing for proven abuse; verification proves a bond exists, not that an agent is honest.
